newsitem.title: USA: Simpson denies new sexual harassment allegations.
newsitem.headline: Simpson denies new sexual harassment allegations.

text.p: O.J. Simpson on Tuesday denied allegations that he had sexually harassed an 18-year-old woman working at the court where he is fighting a wrongful-death civil lawsuit.

A report in USA Today quoted the woman, a part-time paid intern who assists court media-relations officer Jerrianne Hayslett, as saying she was upset and frightened because the former football star had been asking her out on dates.
Simpson told reporters at the Santa Monica courthouse the allegations were untrue. "If I'd have done anything it would be impossible for you people not to see it," he said.

Hayslett, who told USA Today the woman did nothing to encourage Simpson and had been doing "a fabulous job" in helping her, met with Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki in his chambers on Tuesday to discuss the newspaper report. Fujisaki did not refer to the allegations in open court and has sealed a transcript of the closed-door meeting.
The woman, a high school senior, told USA Today Simpson invited her on a Halloween night date last week. The tall blonde was quoted as saying she turned down his invitation.
"Here he is at the trial involving the death of his ex-wife, who he's supposed to be in love with, and he's hitting on me," she was quoted as saying.
Simpson denied making any advances and said he already had a date planned for Halloween night. When asked if he liked the woman, he said: "I don't know her. How would I like her?"

Simpson was found not guilty by a criminal court jury last year of the June 12, 1994, murders of Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman. He is being sued in civil court by the victims' families who are seeking damages.

USA Today also said Simpson appeared to make his interest in the woman plain in the court. The newspaper said once when they accidentally bumped into each other the woman apologised and Simpson said, "You can bump into me anytime you want."
Simpson said on Tuesday he did not recall the incident but added, "That might be something I'd say."
"I can only recall having one brief conversation with her once," Simpson said, adding that on that occasion the woman told him about having aspirations for an acting career.
Hayslett refused comment on the USA Today story.

In testimony Tuesday, Dennis Fung, a police crime-scene expert, testified that preliminary tests conducted at Simpson's home in Brentwood indicated the presence of blood in his sink and shower drains.

Fung said the same tests indicated blood on a wire that hangs behind Simpson's house, near a walkway where a bloody glove was found. But under cross-examination by a lawyer for Simpson, Fung conceded that the material was never confirmed as blood by further testing.
